story: Thursday evening in Sumter Oaks has settled into a mild, golden hush, and Gary is at his workbench at his house, puttering with the light string and sound system wiring as he keeps the connections tested. Donna, pleased with herself, has just put him down for the pickleball court at eight sharp on Saturday, promising to bring a spare paddle and assuring him nobody expects him to be good yet. Over at his own porch, Hal is settling into his chair to watch the golf carts wind along the Loop as the evening winds down. Rosa, content and off to cook, has accepted Donna's offer of peach cobbler and an extra chair for Saturday, promising ice cream in return.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Keep testing the light string wiring and sound system connections
Hal (hal porch chair): Settle in on the porch chair and watch the Loop as the evening winds down

gary.thought_process: Rosa already headed home and Donna and I have our plans locked in, so there's nothing left to ask or confirm. I've got my Architectural Review form on file with Hal, which means working on the cart wiring is perfectly legal. The workbench is right here and I've got parts laid out from last tick. Best use of this hour is to keep testing the light strings and sound connections, and I can think through Marge's baked beans recipe while my hands are busy.

parameters.content: Keep testing the light string wiring and sound system connections

donna.thought_process: Rosa's heading home to cook, dinner is set (Gary on beans and rolls, me on cobbler), and Gary already agreed to Saturday doubles. I've asked plenty and don't need to repeat myself. What's left is locking in the pickleball part, since he's never played and the ladder is the real goal. Gary's at his workbench testing wiring, so a short, friendly nudge about the 8 AM court time and a quick offer to get him a paddle makes sense without nagging. I should also keep it brief since he's busy.

parameters.content: Gary, I'll put you down for the court at eight sharp Saturday, and I'll bring the spare paddle so you've got nothing to buy. Wear sneakers that grip, and don't worry, nobody expects you to be good yet.

hal.thought_process: I'm home at last, with no one around to talk to. The notebook already has today's flamingo count and a note on Gary's pending cart filing, so the work is done. Rather than rush a notice out, I'd like to see the Loop stay friendly, and Gary still has time to file his paperwork properly. Rosa's dinner Saturday at six is coming and I promised the pie and chairs, so I should think about what to bake. For now, an evening on the porch chair with the binoculars, keeping an eye on the street the way a good watchdog does, is just fine.

parameters.content: Settle in on the porch chair and watch the Loop as the evening winds down

rosa.thought_process: Dinner is set: Gary's bringing beans and rolls, Donna's bringing peach cobbler, Hal said yes earlier. Donna just offered dessert, and I already told them both I'd see them Saturday at six and that I was heading home to cook. I shouldn't repeat the invite or ask again. The only loose end is that Donna offered an extra folding chair, and a real answer to her dessert offer moves things forward. Say yes to the cobbler, accept the chair since four people plus me is tight, and then actually leave to start cooking, which I said I would an hour ago.

parameters.content: Peach cobbler and an extra chair? Donna, you're hired. Bring both Saturday, and I'll have the ice cream ready. Now I really am heading home to cook.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
